profile.source: Tomatoes are a familiar food source, while commercial ingredients can have different production routes. No tomato-derived supply has been confirmed.
benefits: Acts as a carotenoid antioxidant in biological research.
Has been investigated for cardiovascular and other health-related outcomes.
profile.evidence: An antioxidant mechanism does not establish prevention or treatment of a disease.
profile.considerations: The tomato illustration is a food association, not a promise about the source or concentration of the final ingredient.

profile.form: Milk thistle extract. Silymarin percentage, extraction method and grade remain unconfirmed.

benefits: Silymarin compounds are investigated for antioxidant activity.

profile.evidence: Results for liver conditions are conflicting or insufficient. A detox or liver-treatment effect is not established.

profile.overview: A fat-soluble vitamin important for vision, immune function and cell differentiation.
profile.form: Vitamin A. Retinol / retinyl esters versus provitamin A carotenoids have not been identified in the current VITA TAPE record.
profile.source: Animal foods supply preformed vitamin A, while carrots and some other plants supply provitamin A carotenoids. The carrot image does not specify a beta-carotene formulation.
benefits: Contributes to normal vision and immune function.
Supports normal skin and cell differentiation.
profile.evidence: Established nutrient roles. Preformed vitamin A and beta-carotene have different safety considerations.
profile.considerations: Excess preformed vitamin A is especially relevant during pregnancy. High-dose beta-carotene is unsuitable for some smokers.
profile.quantityNote: The reference 1600 mcg is retained as listed. Final form and activity-equivalent labelling require confirmation.
